messages.content:
Create a new Godot 4.7 project called ECHOES in the folder echoes. It is a retro neon arcade game for Android phones held in landscape.

Requirements:
1. Use the GL Compatibility renderer on desktop and on mobile.
2. Viewport 384 x 216, stretch mode viewport, aspect expand, so pixels stay sharp on every phone.
3. Default texture filter nearest. Landscape only (sensor landscape). Background colour Color(0.02, 0.01, 0.05).
4. main.tscn has one Node2D that runs scripts/main.gd.
5. Create these scripts, one job each: scripts/game.gd (rules and drawing), scripts/main.gd (menus, HUD, saves), scripts/net.gd (LAN), scripts/art.gd (pixel text), scripts/sound.gd (music and sound).

Everything is drawn in code with _draw(). No image or sound files yet.

The ECHOES project is set up:

Godot 4.7, GL Compatibility renderer on desktop and on mobile
384x216 viewport, stretch mode viewport, aspect expand, so pixels stay sharp on any phone
Landscape only (window/handheld/orientation=4, sensor landscape)
Nearest-neighbour filtering (default_texture_filter=0)
Five scripts, each with one job

Edit scripts/game.gd. Add the arena, the player and the shards.

1. The arena is ARENA = Rect2(-165, -78, 330, 156), centred across the screen and 8 pixels below the middle, to leave room for the HUD. Draw its border magenta and a faint purple grid inside it.
2. The player is a glowing dot with radius 3.5. It speeds up smoothly toward the input direction, up to 92 pixels a second, and stays inside the arena.
3. One gold shard at a time, 5 per level. The player takes it by touching its glow ring, 14 pixels from the centre, not only the diamond.
4. Taking all 5 clears the level. Each level lasts 15 seconds; when the time runs out, the run ends.

Then take a screenshot: godot --path . --resolution 1170x540 -- --shot=/tmp/t.png --shot_at=3 --quit_after_shot

The arena, the player and the shards are in:

Arena 330x156 game pixels, centred, magenta border, purple grid
Player radius 3.5, speed 92 px/s with smooth acceleration
Shards are taken by touching the 14 px glow ring
5 shards clear a level, 15 s per level

Edit scripts/game.gd. This is the heart of the game: your past runs come back.

1. Every physics frame (60 a second), add the player's position to rec, a PackedVector2Array.
2. When a level clears, save rec as a new echo with _add_run(). Keep up to 60 echoes in solo play, so none fade out, and the newest 24 in LAN.
3. function ghost_pos(i, t): where echo i is at level time t.
   - It waits at its first point for a short head start, then replays its path at 60 points a second.
   - At the end of the path it rests at its first point for a moment, then loops.
4. function ghost_live(i, t): true while echo i is moving, false while it waits or rests.
5. Draw each echo as a hollow ring in its own colour. A moving echo that touches the player ends the run. A resting echo can't catch anyone.

Then run the bot: godot --headless --path . -- --autoplay --mode=normal
Reply with the RESULT line.

Echoes work. The bot reached level 12 with 11 of its own past runs on the screen and was caught by the echo from level 3 (killed_by is 0-based).

Edit scripts/game.gd. Add close calls and the score.

1. A close call is a pass: the player comes within 13 pixels of a moving echo, then moves out past 16 pixels. Hovering behind an echo pays nothing.
2. Pay a close call at most once per echo every 2.5 seconds. Remember who is inside in near_in and when it last paid in near_cd.
3. Scores: a shard is 100 x level, a close call is 25 x level, and a level clear adds (seconds left x 20) x level.
4. Keep the local player's points in three counters, sc_shards, sc_close and sc_bonus, for the results screen.

Do not run anything. After the change, stop and reply with one short sentence.

Wrote
scripts/game.gd

Close calls are paid when you pass an echo (in under 13 px, then out past 16 px), at most once per echo every 2.5 s. Hovering behind an echo pays nothing.

Edit scripts/game.gd and scripts/main.gd. Make it feel like an arcade game.

1. The level state goes ready, play, then clear, or dead in solo.
2. Before every level show 3, 2, 1, GO.
3. Taking a shard: a ring, a few particles, a 25 ms buzz and a 0.045 s freeze.
4. Being caught: shake the screen, flash white, freeze for 0.12 s and vibrate for 400 ms.
5. Vibrate only on a phone, and never in the demo game.
6. Show one tip after clearing each of the first four levels:
   after level 1: THAT GHOST IS YOU, FROM LEVEL 1.  DON'T TOUCH IT.
   after level 2: EVERY LEVEL, ONE MORE OF YOU.
   after level 3: KEEP YOUR PATH TIDY: EVERY MOVE COMES BACK.
   after level 4: BRUSH PAST THEM FOR BONUS POINTS.
7. TRY AGAIN on the results screen starts a new run. A stray tap anywhere else does nothing, so nobody loses their results by accident.

Create the file shaders/crt.gdshader, a canvas_item shader that makes the screen look like an old arcade monitor.

1. Read the screen with hint_screen_texture.
2. A slight colour fringe: offset red and blue by 0.0005, more while the uniform shake is above 0.
3. A cheap glow: average 8 nearby taps and add whatever is brighter than 0.4.
4. Scanlines: every second row at 0.9 brightness.
5. A vignette of strength 0.4, and a white flash from the uniform flash.

Put it on a full-screen ColorRect in a CanvasLayer at layer 20 in scripts/main.gd. Add CRT ON/OFF to Settings, saved as save["crt"].

Colours for the game: near-black background, the player white-hot with a cyan ring and a comet trail, echoes as hollow rings, shards gold. In solo play echo colours are never cyan or gold; in LAN games each echo takes its owner's colour.

Create tools/make_audio.py. It renders the whole soundtrack and every sound effect as WAV files, so the game has no outside sound files.

1. Synthwave chiptune: detuned saw and pulse leads, a saw bass with a filter envelope, an 80s gated snare, noise risers, and a sidechain pump on the pad and the bass.
2. Tracks: music_title.wav, music_game.wav, music_intense.wav and jingle_gameover.wav.
3. Sound effects: sfx_shard1.wav to sfx_shard5.wav (one step higher for each shard in a level), sfx_close, sfx_death, sfx_clear, sfx_spawn, sfx_tick, sfx_select, sfx_move, sfx_go and sfx_best.
4. 16-bit mono PCM at 32000 Hz, written to assets/audio/. Music loops must be exactly periodic and carry a RIFF smpl loop chunk, so Godot loops them without a click.
5. Check every file: peak level, rms, no clipping, and the loop seam.

Then run: python3 tools/make_audio.py --no-png

   - TILT + TOUCH: tilt picks the direction, holding a finger anywhere is the accelerator, lifting it stops.
   - Arrow keys and WASD always work too, for testing on a computer.

On the Galaxy S25 Ultra tilt first read zero: Godot 4.7 has the sensors off unless sensors/enable_accelerometer and sensors/enable_gravity are on. With them on, both axes came out reversed on that phone, which the next prompt fixes.

Edit scripts/main.gd. Sensor axes differ between phones, so add a three-step tilt calibration.

1. The steps: hold the phone the way you play and tap START; tip the right side down and hold it; go back to how you started; tip the far edge away and hold it.
2. _calib_tick(): a tip counts once it is held for 0.45 s, and the return to the start once it is held for 0.3 s. If the second tip goes the same way as the first, start again.
3. Save the direction the phone reported for "right" as save["tilt_r"] and for "away" as save["tilt_u"], each as three numbers.
4. In _tilt(), when both are saved, the move direction is how far gravity has moved along tilt_r (left and right) and along tilt_u (up and down). Then apply INVERT X / Y, divide by the tilt speed (4.2, 2.8 or 1.8), ignore anything under 0.12, and cap it at 1.
5. Open calibration on its own the first time a tilt control is picked (_pick_control()).

Write scripts/net.gd for LAN play like the old Mini Militia: one phone hosts, and friends on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot join.

1. const PORT := 47010, const DISC_PORT := 47011, const MAGIC := "ECHOES1"
2. function host(): an ENet server on PORT for 7 more players, and a UDP socket with broadcast turned on.
3. function join(ip): an ENet client to ip on PORT.
4. The host announces itself once a second, as MAGIC|name|players|open, to 255.255.255.255 and to every local subnet. Turn broadcast on for the listener too, so Android takes its multicast lock.
5. JOIN LAN lists the hosts it hears. ENTER ADDRESS opens a keypad and remembers the last address.
6. The host sends snapshot() 30 times a second.

Then test discovery with --listen_test, and start a host with --host --players=3.

Edit scripts/game.gd. In LAN games a caught player isn't out: they come back as a ZOMBIE, still steered by that person.

1. Zombies are squares in toxic yellow-green, Color(0.78, 1.0, 0.12), with teeth. They move at 90% of human speed, pass through echoes and can't take shards.
2. Touching a person turns them into a zombie and gives the zombie 300 x level.
3. A new zombie blinks for 1.5 s before it can catch anyone.
4. Zombies start each level on the far side of the arena (spawn_pos()).
5. function zombie_touching(id): the victim judges the catch on their own screen. Return the first zombie, past its 1.5 s, closer than two player radii plus 1 pixel, or -1.
6. The last human standing wins.
